# Check catalogue

<!-- Generated by `python -m ap2_evidence.checksdoc`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every report contains exactly one result for each check below. Statuses are PASS, FAIL, WARN and SKIP. The verdict is FAILED if any check FAILs, otherwise INCOMPLETE if any *required* check is SKIP, otherwise VERIFIED. WARN never changes the verdict.

"Required" is the default; a result can be marked not required when the check does not apply (for example aud/nonce when no expected value was supplied, or key-binding checks for a directly signed one-segment mandate).

Spec references are paths in the upstream repository github.com/google-agentic-commerce/AP2 at commit e1ea56db72a6385bce3e5c1112b3a56ce60acb43.

Every non-PASS result also carries a machine-readable `reason` code (listed in docs/output-formats.md).

86 checks.

## Bundle

| ID | Check | Required | Worst | What it checks | What this check is for | Spec reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B01 | Bundle readable | yes | FAIL | The input is a JSON object with bundle_version 'ap2-evidence/1' and members of the expected types. Unknown members are ignored with a warning. | Confirms that the input is an evidence bundle this tool can read; without this, nothing can be checked. | docs/bundle-format.md (this tool) |
| B02 | All four artifacts present | yes | FAIL | checkout_mandate, payment_mandate, checkout_receipt and payment_receipt are present. | Confirms that all four documents of the dispute chain are present; each missing one leaves a link of the chain unproven. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Dispute Evidence" |
| B03 | Supplied keys are valid | yes | FAIL | Every key under keys.* (and --trusted-keys) is a P-256 public JWK; roles are mandate_issuer, merchant, payment_processor. | Confirms that the supplied keys are well-formed public keys; a malformed or private key signals a careless or manipulated bundle. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/types/jwk.json |

## Checkout mandate chain

| ID | Check | Required | Worst | What it checks | What this check is for | Spec reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CM01 | Checkout mandate chain parses | yes | FAIL | The token splits into '~~'-joined SD-JWT segments; each segment is a compact JWS with canonical base64url, JSON-object header and payload (no duplicate keys) and well-formed disclosures. | Confirms that the token can be read at all. Without this, nothing else can be checked; a token that does not parse is often a truncated or hand-edited copy. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/README.md (chain serialization); RFC 9901 section 4 |
| CM02 | Root token algorithm is ES256 | yes | FAIL | The 'alg' header of the root (issuer-signed) token is ES256. 'none', HMAC (HS*) and EdDSA are rejected; this version verifies ES256 / P-256 only. | Confirms that the signature algorithm is fixed. Without this, an attacker who can choose the algorithm could make a forged token 'verify'. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/types/jwk.json (alg ES256); docs/ap2/specification.md "Payment Mandate" (no deterministic signatures) |
| CM03 | Root token signature (mandate issuer) | yes | FAIL | The root token's signature verifies under a key of role 'mandate_issuer' (the user's credential or the trusted agent provider), matched by 'kid' when present. | Confirms that the mandate comes from the user or their agent provider. Without this, the open mandate's limits and agent key could have been written by anyone. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Modes"; docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Verification and Processing Rules" |
| CM04 | Root token disclosures resolve | yes | FAIL | Every disclosure of the root segment is referenced exactly once by a digest in the signed payload (directly or recursively), no digest repeats, _sd_alg is sha-256/384/512, and delegate_payload resolves to one mandate object. | Confirms that every disclosed part of the open mandate was issued with it. Without this, a part could have been swapped or added later, e.g. to show a different allowed merchant. | RFC 9901 section 7.1; code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/chain.py (delegate_payload) |
| CM05 | Open mandate type (vct) | yes | FAIL | The root mandate object's vct is exactly 'mandate.checkout.open.1' (two-segment chain). | Confirms that the open mandate is the type it is presented as. The type (vct) selects the schema and the meaning of its limits; implementations MUST match the exact string including the version suffix. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Mandate Versioning"; docs/ap2/checkout_mandate.md "Type" |
| CM06 | Open mandate binds an agent key (cnf.jwk) | yes | FAIL | The open mandate carries cnf.jwk and it is a valid EC P-256 public key with only the members allowed by AP2 jwk.json. | Confirms that the open mandate names the one agent key allowed to act on it (cnf.jwk). Without this, any key could sign the closed mandate. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Autonomous (Human Not Present)"; code/sdk/schemas/ap2/types/jwk.json |
| CM07 | Closed token type is kb+sd-jwt | yes | FAIL | The closed (agent-signed) token's 'typ' header is 'kb+sd-jwt'. The spelling 'kb-sd-jwt' is accepted with a warning, as the upstream SDK does. | Confirms that the closed token is marked as an agent-signed (key-binding) step. Without this, a root token could be replayed as a closed mandate. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/kb_sd_jwt.py (TYP_TERMINAL) |
| CM08 | Closed mandate signed by the bound agent key | yes | FAIL | The closed token is ES256 and its signature verifies under the open mandate's cnf.jwk (key binding / proof of possession). | Confirms that the agent the user authorised - and nobody else - approved this specific transaction. | docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Mandate Structure" (Closed); kb_sd_jwt.py verify() |
| CM09 | Closed token is bound to the open token (sd_hash) | yes | FAIL | The closed token carries exactly one of sd_hash / issuer_jwt_hash, and it equals the hash of the open segment exactly as presented. | Confirms that the closed mandate was made for this open mandate. Without this, the agent's signature could be moved onto a different open mandate with other limits. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/common.py verify_binding() |
| CM10 | Closed token disclosures resolve | yes | FAIL | Every disclosure of the closed segment is referenced exactly once by a digest in the agent-signed payload, and delegate_payload resolves to one mandate object. | Confirms that every disclosed part of the closed mandate was signed by the agent. Without this, content could have been swapped after the agent signed it. | RFC 9901 section 7.1 |
| CM11 | Closed mandate type (vct) | yes | FAIL | The closed mandate object's vct is exactly 'mandate.checkout.1'. | Confirms that the closed token is the mandate it is presented as. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Mandate Versioning"; docs/ap2/checkout_mandate.md "Type" |
| CM12 | Closed mandate carries no cnf | yes | FAIL | A closed mandate presented as a key-binding hop (two segments) has no 'cnf' claim. A directly signed one-segment mandate may carry cnf (upstream has no such rule for a root token). | Confirms that the closed mandate cannot be passed on. A cnf there would let the holder of that key delegate further; AP2 v0.2 closed mandates are terminal. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/kb_sd_jwt.py (a terminal key-binding hop MUST NOT carry cnf); sdjwt/chain.py (no cnf rule for the root token) |
| CM13 | Closed mandate fields and types | yes | FAIL | All fields required by code/sdk/schemas/ap2/checkout_mandate.json are present with the right JSON types (integers for amounts and timestamps). | Confirms that the mandate has every required field with the right type. Without this, the mandate is ambiguous as evidence. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/checkout_mandate.json |
| CM14 | Audience (aud) as expected | yes | FAIL | The closed token's 'aud' equals expected.<kind>.aud from the bundle, when given. | Confirms that the agent presented the mandate to the expected recipient (aud), not to a different verifier. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/common.py verify_expected_claims() |
| CM15 | Nonce as expected | yes | FAIL | The closed token's 'nonce' equals expected.<kind>.nonce from the bundle, when given. | Confirms that the presentation belongs to the expected verifier session (nonce). Without this, an old presentation could be replayed. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/common.py verify_expected_claims() |
| CM16 | Chronology of open and closed mandate | yes | FAIL | The closed token has an integer iat that lies within the open mandate's iat..exp window (with clock skew), and the open mandate's iat is not after its exp. | Confirms that the agent signed while the user's authorisation was in force: not before the open mandate was issued and not after it expired. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/chain.py _check_time_claims(); this tool's design |
| CM17 | All constraint types are known | yes | FAIL | Every constraint in the open mandate has a type defined for this mandate in AP2 v0.2. | Confirms that every limit in the mandate is one this tool understands. Unknown constraints MUST be treated as failing: the user may have set a limit this verifier cannot see. | docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Verification and Processing Rules" step 3 |
| CM18 | Pre-set claims unchanged | yes | FAIL | Every claim the open mandate fixes in advance (anything other than vct, constraints, cnf, iat, exp) appears unchanged in the closed mandate. | Confirms that the agent did not change anything the user fixed in advance (for example the payee or the amount). | docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Verification and Processing Rules" step 2 |
| CM19 | Valid at the --at instant | no | FAIL | Only with --at: the open mandate's iat..exp window (and any closed exp) contains the given instant. | Answers 'was this mandate valid at time T?'. Without --at, wall-clock expiry is deliberately not checked because dispute evidence is always expired now. | code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/sdjwt/chain.py _check_time_claims() |
| CM20 | Chain shape supported | yes | SKIP | One segment (directly signed closed mandate) or two segments (open + closed). Longer chains are agent-to-agent delegation, outside AP2 v0.2, and are not verified. | Confirms that every delegation step in the token is one this tool verifies; steps it does not verify cannot be part of the proof. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Agent-to-Agent Delegation" |
| CM21 | Open mandate fields and types | yes | FAIL | The open mandate's fields have the types required by code/sdk/schemas/ap2/open_checkout_mandate.json (constraints is an array of objects with a string type and well-typed fields, iat/exp integers, pre-set claims well-formed). A missing constraint that the schema expects is a warning. | Confirms that the open mandate's limits are well-formed. Without this, they cannot be evaluated reliably. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/open_checkout_mandate.json |
| CM22 | No withheld constraints or claims | yes | FAIL | No constraint of the open mandate is withheld (an undisclosed element of the constraints array FAILs), and no claim of the open or closed mandate object or of a constraint is withheld (an _sd digest without its disclosure is SKIP: the mandate must be supplied with all its disclosures as issued). Undisclosed entries of 'allowed' / 'acceptable_items' are fine: they only narrow what is allowed. | Confirms that no limit or claim was withheld from the bundle. Without this, an agent could drop a disclosure to hide a limit the user set (an amount range, the allowed items, a pre-set amount) and still bind its signature to what it presents. | docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Verification and Processing Rules" step 3; RFC 9901 section 4.2.5 (decoys) |
| CM30 | Merchant checkout JWT readable | yes | FAIL | The closed checkout mandate discloses checkout_jwt, and it is a compact JWS with alg ES256 and a JSON-object payload. | Confirms that the merchant's signed statement of what is being sold (the checkout JWT) is present and readable. | docs/ap2/checkout_mandate.md "Mandate Schema"; docs/ap2/specification.md "Payment Mandate" (no deterministic signatures) |
| CM31 | checkout_hash matches the checkout JWT | yes | FAIL | checkout_hash equals base64url(SHA-256(ASCII bytes of checkout_jwt)). | Confirms that the agent's signature covers exactly the merchant's checkout shown in the bundle. Without this, the agent could have approved a different checkout. | docs/ap2/checkout_mandate.md "Mandate Schema" (checkout_hash); docs/ap2/specification.md "Dispute" |
| CM32 | Checkout JWT signature (merchant) | yes | FAIL | The checkout JWT's signature verifies under a key of role 'merchant'. | Confirms that the merchant itself issued the checkout (items, prices, total). | docs/ap2/specification.md "Checkout Mandate" (merchant-signed JWT) |
| CM33 | Checkout payload is a UCP Checkout | yes | FAIL | The checkout JWT payload has the UCP Checkout members (id, line_items, status, currency, totals, links) with valid types. A non-UCP payload is a warning and the UCP-dependent checks are skipped. | Confirms that the checkout is a UCP Checkout, the format the item, merchant and total checks are defined for. | code/sdk/schemas/ucp/types/checkout.json; docs/ap2/specification.md "Checkout Object" |
| CM34 | Constraint checkout.allowed_merchants | yes | FAIL | The checkout's merchant is among the revealed 'allowed' entries (by id when both have one, else name + website). No revealed entries fails. | Confirms that the user allowed purchases from this merchant. | docs/ap2/checkout_mandate.md "Allowed Merchants" |
| CM35 | Constraint checkout.line_items | yes | FAIL | Every checkout item can be assigned to a requirement whose revealed acceptable_items contain its id, within each requirement's quantity (max-flow, as the upstream SDK). | Confirms that the agent bought only items the user allowed, in allowed quantities. | docs/ap2/checkout_mandate.md "Line Items"; code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/max_flow_helper.py |

## Cross-artifact consistency

| ID | Check | Required | Worst | What it checks | What this check is for | Spec reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XC01 | Paid amount equals the checkout total | yes | FAIL | payment_amount (amount and currency) equals the checkout JWT's totals[type=total].amount and currency. | Confirms that the amount paid equals the total of the merchant's signed checkout. | code/sdk/schemas/ucp/types/checkout.json (totals); this tool's design |
| XC02 | Payee equals the checkout merchant | yes | FAIL | The payment mandate's payee matches the checkout JWT's merchant (by id when both have one, else name + website). | Confirms that the money went to the merchant that sold the goods. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/payment_mandate.json (payee); this tool's design |
| XC03 | Both mandates bind the same agent key | no | WARN | The open checkout and open payment mandates carry the same cnf.jwk (compared by RFC 7638 thumbprint). Not normative: a warning only. | Flags checkout and payment approved by different agent keys: allowed, but unusual and worth a look. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Autonomous (Human Not Present)" |
| XC04 | Both mandates signed by the same mandate-issuer key | no | WARN | The root tokens of the checkout and payment mandate chains verified under the same mandate_issuer key (compared by RFC 7638 thumbprint). Advisory: a warning only. | Flags mandates issued under different issuer keys. The tool cannot tell which key belongs to which user or agent provider, and two different issuer keys can mean that the checkout and the payment were authorised by different people (for example one user's checkout paid with another user's card). | docs/ap2/specification.md "Modes"; this tool's design |
| EX01 | Agent key as expected | no | FAIL | When an expected agent key (public JWK) is given: the cnf.jwk the closed mandates are bound to has the same RFC 7638 thumbprint. | Confirms that the mandates were closed by the agent the relying party dealt with, not by another agent holding a valid delegation. | verify_bundle(expected=...) (this tool; the relying party's own expectations) |
| EX02 | Checkout id as expected | no | FAIL | When an expected checkout id is given: it equals the id in the merchant-signed checkout. | Confirms that the evidence is about the checkout the relying party means. | verify_bundle(expected=...) (this tool; the relying party's own expectations) |
| EX03 | Merchant id as expected | no | FAIL | When an expected merchant id is given: it equals the merchant id in the checkout and the payee id in the closed payment mandate. | Confirms that the evidence is about the merchant the relying party means. | verify_bundle(expected=...) (this tool; the relying party's own expectations) |
| EX04 | Total as expected | no | FAIL | When an expected total is given: it equals the checkout total and the paid amount (amount in minor units and currency). | Confirms that the amount is the one the relying party expects. | verify_bundle(expected=...) (this tool; the relying party's own expectations) |
| EX05 | Required constraints present | no | FAIL | When required constraint types are given: the open mandates carry a constraint of each type. | Confirms that the user's mandate actually limited the agent in the ways the relying party requires (for example an amount range). | verify_bundle(expected=...) (this tool; the relying party's own expectations) |

## Checkout receipt

| ID | Check | Required | Worst | What it checks | What this check is for | Spec reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CR01 | Checkout receipt parses | yes | FAIL | The receipt is a plain compact JWT (not an SD-JWT) with alg ES256 and JSON-object header and payload. | Confirms that the receipt can be read; a receipt that does not parse proves nothing. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/checkout_receipt.json; docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Action Authorization" (Verifier-signed JWT) |
| CR02 | Checkout receipt signature (merchant) | yes | FAIL | The receipt's signature verifies under a key of role 'merchant'. | Confirms that the merchant issued this receipt. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Checkout Mandate" |
| CR03 | Checkout receipt fields | yes | FAIL | Fields required by code/sdk/schemas/ap2/checkout_receipt.json for the receipt's status are present with the right types (null members tolerated). The prose variant 'result: success\|error' is accepted with a warning. | Confirms that the receipt carries the identifiers needed to match it with the issuer's records. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/checkout_receipt.json; docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Action Authorization" |
| CR04 | Checkout receipt references the closed mandate | yes | FAIL | reference equals SHA-256 of the closed mandate's issuer-signed JWT (upstream SDK form) or the sd_hash-form hash of the final segment (prose form, noted). | Confirms that the receipt is for this mandate and not for some other transaction. | docs/ap2/specification.md "Dispute"; code/sdk/python/ap2/sdk/mandate.py get_closed_mandate_jwt() |
| CR05 | Checkout receipt outcome | yes | FAIL | Reads the outcome the receipt states (status 'Success' / 'Error', or the prose form's result 'success' / 'error'). Success passes; an error is a WARN saying the step was declined; a success that also carries an error FAILs. The outcome is used for the report's outcome only if the receipt's signature, required fields, reference and time checks passed. | Confirms that the step was completed; a rejection receipt documents that it did not happen. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/types/receipt_status.json |
| CR06 | Checkout receipt not earlier than the mandate | yes | FAIL | The receipt's iat is not earlier than the closed mandate's iat minus the clock skew. | Confirms that the receipt was issued after the mandate it answers; a receipt issued before the mandate existed cannot be a response to it. | this tool's design (chronology is not defined upstream) |
| CR07 | Checkout receipt issuer plausible | no | WARN | Advisory: iss equals (or has the same host as) the checkout merchant's website. A warning only: iss is self-declared, so it does not decide whether the receipt counts for the report's outcome (that rests on the signature, required fields, reference and time checks). | Flags a receipt from an unexpected issuer, which deserves a closer look at who signed it. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/checkout_receipt.json (iss) |

The prose variant 'result: success\|error' is accepted with a warning. | Confirms that the receipt carries the identifiers needed to match it with the issuer's records. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/payment_receipt.json; docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md "Action Authorization" |

The outcome is used for the report's outcome only if the receipt's signature, required fields, reference and time checks passed. | Confirms that the step was completed; a rejection receipt documents that it did not happen. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/types/receipt_status.json |
| PR06 | Payment receipt not earlier than the mandate | yes | FAIL | The receipt's iat is not earlier than the closed mandate's iat minus the clock skew. | Confirms that the receipt was issued after the mandate it answers; a receipt issued before the mandate existed cannot be a response to it. | this tool's design (chronology is not defined upstream) |

A warning only: iss is self-declared, so it does not decide whether the receipt counts for the report's outcome (that rests on the signature, required fields, reference and time checks). | Flags a receipt from an unexpected issuer, which deserves a closer look at who signed it. | code/sdk/schemas/ap2/payment_receipt.json (iss) |

## Reason codes in plain words

Reports put the plain sentence before the technical detail of a non-PASS result and build the 'What to do next' list from the next steps. In the wording, `{doc}` is the document the check is about, `{party}` who can supply or explain it, `{signer}` whose signature the check verifies and `{kind}` is checkout or payment. A code without a next step needs no action.

| Reason | Plain wording | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blocked` | This check could not run because an earlier check it depends on did not pass. | - |
| `missing_artifact` | {doc} is not in the bundle. | Ask {party} for {doc}. |
| `not_applicable` | This check does not apply to this input. | - |
| `no_key` | The {signer}'s signature could not be checked because no public key of the {signer} was supplied. | Get the {signer}'s public key directly from the {signer} (not from the bundle) and check again with {keyopt} FILE (or --trusted-keys FILE). |
| `x5c_unsupported` | The {signer}'s signature relies on a certificate chain (x5c), which this version cannot check. | Get the {signer}'s public key itself from a source you trust and re-run with --trusted-keys. |
| `internal_error` | This check could not be evaluated on this input. | Check {doc} by hand and report the problem to the ap2-evidence maintainers (with test data only). |
| `unspecified` | This check did not pass. | - |
| `parse_error` | {doc} cannot be read: it is damaged, truncated or not in the expected format. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `alg_not_allowed` | {doc} uses a signature algorithm this tool does not accept. | Ask {party} why {doc} is not signed with ES256. |
| `signature_invalid` | The {signer}'s signature on {doc} does not verify: another key signed it, or it was changed after signing. | Get the {signer}'s public key directly from the {signer} (not from the bundle) and check again with {keyopt} FILE (or --trusted-keys FILE). If it still fails, ask the {signer} whether it issued {doc}. |
| `unreferenced_disclosure` | Part of {doc} was replaced or added after it was issued: one of its disclosures matches nothing the {signer} signed. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `duplicate_disclosure` | {doc} presents the same disclosure twice, which an unmodified token never does. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `digest_reused` | {doc} uses the same digest twice, which a correctly issued token never does. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `disclosure_kind_mismatch` | {doc} is not a well-formed selective-disclosure token. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `claim_collision` | {doc} is not a well-formed selective-disclosure token: a disclosed claim clashes with a signed one. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `bad_digest` | {doc} is not a well-formed selective-disclosure token. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `sd_not_array` | {doc} is not a well-formed selective-disclosure token. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `nested_too_deep` | {doc} is nested more deeply than this tool evaluates. | Check {doc} by hand or ask {party} why it is nested this deeply. |
| `unsupported_sd_alg` | {doc} uses a hash algorithm for its disclosures that this tool does not support. | Ask {party} which hash algorithm was used and check {doc} by other means. |
| `unresolvable` | The content of {doc} could not be read. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `no_mandate_object` | {doc} contains no readable mandate. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `multiple_mandate_objects` | {doc} contains more than one mandate, so it is unclear which one was approved. | Ask {party} which mandate was actually approved. |
| `wrong_vct` | {doc} is not the type of mandate it is presented as. | Ask {party} for the right {doc}. |
| `no_cnf_jwk` | The open {kind} mandate does not name the agent key allowed to act for the user. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `invalid_cnf_jwk` | The agent key named in the open {kind} mandate is not a valid key. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `wrong_typ` | {doc} is not marked as an agent-signed mandate. | Ask {party} for the right {doc}. |
| `intermediate_typ` | {doc} is marked as an intermediate delegation step, not as the final agent-signed mandate. | Ask {party} for the final agent-signed {kind} mandate. |
| `typ_variant` | {doc} uses a variant spelling of its token type; it was accepted, as the official SDK does. | - |
| `binding_claim_count` | The closed {kind} mandate does not name exactly one open mandate it belongs to. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `binding_mismatch` | The closed {kind} mandate was made for a different open mandate than the one in the bundle, or that open mandate was changed afterwards. | Ask the agent provider for the open {kind} mandate exactly as its agent received it. |
| `cnf_in_closed` | The closed {kind} mandate names a further key that could act on it, which AP2 v0.2 does not allow. | Ask the agent provider why the closed {kind} mandate delegates further. |
| `missing_field` | {doc} lacks a field it must have. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `wrong_type` | {doc} has a field with the wrong type of value. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `aud_mismatch` | {doc} was presented to a different recipient than expected. | Confirm the expected recipient (aud); if it is right, ask the agent provider why the mandate was made for someone else. |
| `nonce_mismatch` | {doc} belongs to a different session than expected, which can mean it was replayed. | Confirm the expected nonce; if it is right, ask the agent provider why the mandate carries another one. |
| `no_expected_value` | No expected value was given, so this was not compared. | - |
| `no_kb_iat` | The closed {kind} mandate has no signing time. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `iat_not_integer` | The closed {kind} mandate has no usable signing time. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `signed_before_open` | The agent signed the closed {kind} mandate before the user's open mandate was issued. | Ask the agent provider why its agent signed before the user's authorisation existed. |
| `signed_after_expiry` | The agent signed the closed {kind} mandate after the user's open mandate had expired. | Ask the agent provider why its agent acted after the user's authorisation expired. |
| `open_iat_after_exp` | The open {kind} mandate expires before it was issued, so it was never valid. | Ask the mandate issuer why the open {kind} mandate was issued with these dates. |
| `after_closed_exp` | The {kind} mandate had already expired at the time given with --at. | Confirm the --at time; if it is right, the mandate was not valid at that time. |
| `not_valid_at` | The {kind} mandate was not valid at the time given with --at. | Confirm the --at time; if it is right, the mandate was not valid at that time. |
| `no_at` | No --at time was given, so validity at a given time was not checked. | - |
| `delegation_unsupported` | {doc} passes the authority through more than one agent, which this tool does not verify. | Check the extra delegation steps of {doc} by other means. |
| `unknown_constraint_type` | The user's mandate contains a limit of a type this tool does not know, so it cannot confirm the limit was respected. | Ask the agent provider what the unknown limit means and check it by hand. |
| `preset_claim_changed` | The agent changed a value the user fixed in advance in the open {kind} mandate. | Ask the agent provider why its agent changed a value the user had fixed. |
| `malformed_constraint` | A limit in the user's {kind} mandate is malformed, so it cannot be evaluated. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `missing_required_constraint` | The user's {kind} mandate lacks a limit its schema expects. | Ask the agent provider whether the open {kind} mandate was issued without this limit. |
| `no_constraints` | The user's {kind} mandate contains no limits at all. | - |
| `hidden_constraint` | A limit in the user's {kind} mandate was withheld from the bundle, so it cannot be checked. | Ask the agent provider for the open {kind} mandate with all of its disclosures as issued. |
| `withheld_claim` | Part of {doc} was withheld from the bundle, so it is unclear whether it limits the agent. | Ask the agent provider for the {kind} mandate with all of its disclosures as issued. |
| `no_constraint` | The user's mandate sets no limit of this type. | - |
| `none_revealed` | The bundle shows none of the entries the user allowed, so it cannot show that this one was allowed. | Ask the agent provider for the open {kind} mandate with all of its disclosures as issued. |
| `merchant_not_allowed` | The merchant is not one of the merchants the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `payee_not_allowed` | The payee is not one of the payees the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `item_not_acceptable` | The checkout contains an item the user did not allow. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `quantity_exceeded` | The checkout contains more of an item than the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `requirement_unfilled` | The checkout does not contain an item the user's mandate requires. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `too_many_lines` | The checkout has more lines than this tool evaluates. | Check the items by hand. |
| `amount_above_max` | The payment is larger than the maximum the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved a payment above the user's limit. |
| `amount_below_min` | The payment is smaller than the minimum the user set. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `currency_mismatch` | The payment is in a different currency than the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `instrument_not_allowed` | The payment uses a card or account the user did not allow. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `no_instrument` | The payment mandate does not say which card or account was used. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `pisp_not_allowed` | The payment goes through a payment initiation provider the user did not allow. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `no_pisp` | The payment mandate does not name the payment initiation provider the user's limit refers to. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `execution_date_before_window` | The payment is scheduled before the dates the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `execution_date_after_window` | The payment is scheduled after the dates the user allowed. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved this although the user's mandate does not allow it. |
| `malformed_mandate` | {doc} has a malformed value that this check needs. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `budget_exceeded` | This payment alone exceeds the user's whole budget. | Ask the agent provider why its agent approved a payment above the user's budget. |
| `recurrence_malformed` | The user's rule for repeated payments is malformed, so it cannot limit repeated use. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `recurrence_missing_companion` | The user's rule for repeated payments lacks the amount or budget limit it needs. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `cumulative_unverifiable` | Whether the user's total budget or repeat limit was respected depends on the other payments made under this mandate, which one bundle does not contain. | Ask the agent provider for all other payments made under the same open payment mandate. |
| `checkout_jwt_missing` | The checkout mandate does not contain the merchant's signed checkout. | Ask the agent provider for the checkout mandate including the merchant's signed checkout. |
| `not_jws` | {doc} is not a readable signed token. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `payload_not_object` | The content of {doc} cannot be read. | Ask {party} for a complete, unmodified copy of {doc}. |
| `hash_mismatch` | The checkout the agent approved is not the merchant's checkout shown in the bundle. | Ask the agent provider and the merchant for the checkout the agent actually approved. |
| `checkout_hash_missing` | The checkout mandate does not say which checkout the agent approved. | Ask {party} for {doc} exactly as it was issued, with all of its disclosures. |
| `not_ascii` | The merchant's signed checkout contains characters that make its fingerprint ambiguous. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `malformed_checkout` | The merchant's checkout has malformed parts; only its readable parts were used. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `not_ucp` | The merchant's checkout is not in the standard UCP Checkout format; only its readable parts were used. | - |
| `no_merchant` | The merchant's checkout does not say who the merchant is. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `merchant_unreadable` | The merchant cannot be identified from the checkout. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `line_items_unreadable` | The purchased items cannot be read from the merchant's checkout. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `transaction_id_mismatch` | The payment mandate is for a different checkout than the one in the bundle. | Ask the agent provider which checkout this payment was for. |
| `checkout_hash_mismatch` | The payment mandate and the checkout mandate refer to different checkouts. | Ask the agent provider which checkout this payment was for. |
| `reference_mismatch` | {doc} refers to a different document than the one in the bundle. | Ask {party} for the version of {doc} that belongs to the documents in this bundle. |
| `issuer_jwt_form_with_withheld` | The link between the payment and checkout authorisations can only be confirmed with the complete open checkout mandate. | Ask the agent provider for the open checkout mandate with all of its disclosures as issued. |
| `amount_mismatch` | The amount paid differs from the total of the merchant's signed checkout. | Ask the agent provider why the amount paid differs from the merchant's checkout total. |
| `negative_total` | The total of the merchant's checkout is negative. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `no_single_total` | The merchant's checkout does not state one total. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `total_unreadable` | The total cannot be read from the merchant's checkout. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout as issued. |
| `payee_mismatch` | The money went to a different payee than the merchant in the signed checkout. | Ask the agent provider why the payee differs from the merchant that sold the goods. |
| `agent_key_differs` | The checkout and the payment were approved by different agent keys. | Ask the agent provider why two different agent keys were used. |
| `issuer_key_differs` | The checkout and payment mandates were issued under different keys, which can mean that different people authorised them. | Find out who holds each mandate-issuer key before relying on the bundle. |
| `sd_jwt_receipt` | {doc} is in the wrong format (a selective-disclosure token, not a plain signed receipt). | Ask {party} for {doc} as a plain signed receipt. |
| `conflicting_outcome` | {doc} states both success and failure. | Ask {party} what the outcome actually was. |
| `prose_receipt_form` | {doc} uses the form described in the AP2 prose rather than the official SDK; it was accepted. | - |
| `rejected` | {doc} says the transaction was rejected. | Ask {party} whether the transaction was completed later; this receipt documents a rejection. |
| `receipt_before_mandate` | {doc} was issued before the mandate it answers existed. | Ask {party} why its receipt predates the mandate. |
| `issuer_mismatch` | {doc} was issued by an unexpected party. | Check who issued {doc}. |
| `not_object` | The input is not an evidence bundle. | Ask whoever supplied the bundle for it in the documented bundle format. |
| `bad_version` | The bundle is not in a format version this tool reads. | Ask whoever supplied the bundle for it in the documented bundle format. |
| `bad_member_type` | An entry of the bundle has the wrong type. | Ask whoever supplied the bundle for it in the documented bundle format. |
| `too_long` | An entry of the bundle is longer than this tool accepts. | Check the bundle by hand; ask whoever supplied it why the entry is this long. |
| `unknown_member` | The bundle contains an entry this tool does not know; it was ignored. | Check the bundle's entry names for typos. |
| `no_artifacts` | The bundle contains none of the four documents. | Ask whoever supplied the bundle for the mandates and receipts. |
| `invalid_key` | A key supplied with the bundle or with --trusted-keys is not a valid public key. | Replace the invalid key with the party's public key from a source you trust. |
| `unknown_role` | A key was supplied for a role this tool does not know; it was ignored. | Check the role names of the supplied keys. |
| `no_keys` | No public keys were supplied, so no signature of the mandate issuer, merchant or payment processor could be checked. | Get the public keys directly from the mandate issuer, the merchant and the payment processor and check again with --issuer-key, --merchant-key and --processor-key (or --trusted-keys FILE). |
| `key_not_pinned` | The {signer}'s signature was not checked with a pinned key (one you gave this tool with --trusted-keys), as was required. | Get the {signer}'s public key directly from the {signer} (not from the bundle) and check again with {keyopt} FILE (or --trusted-keys FILE). |
| `payee_details_differ` | The payee in the agent-signed payment mandate has the merchant's id but a different name or website than the merchant-signed checkout. | Ask the agent provider why the payee's name or website differs from the merchant's own checkout, and confirm with the merchant who was paid. |
| `merchant_details_differ` | The merchant in the merchant-signed checkout has the id of a merchant the user allowed, but a different name or website than the user's mandate gives for it. | Confirm with the merchant the user allowed that this checkout is theirs, and ask the agent provider why the agent accepted a merchant whose name or website differs. |
| `success_with_error` | {doc} says Success but also carries an error code, so its outcome is unclear. | Ask {party} what the outcome of the transaction actually was. |
| `checkout_canceled` | The merchant's signed checkout is marked as canceled. | Ask the merchant whether this checkout was canceled and whether the payment was refunded. |
| `checkout_not_final` | The merchant's signed checkout is not marked as ready or completed. | Ask the merchant whether this checkout was final when the agent approved it. |
| `reference_unverifiable_withheld` | The user's payment authorisation does not match the checkout instructions as they appear in this bundle. That is what checkout instructions shown with some parts left out look like, and also what a payment authorisation for a different checkout looks like; this bundle cannot tell the two apart. | Ask the agent provider for the open checkout mandate exactly as issued, with all of its disclosures, and check again. |
| `history_currency_mismatch` | The earlier total you supplied is in a different currency than the user's budget, so the two cannot be added up. | Supply the earlier total in the budget's currency with --prior-total MINOR_UNITS CURRENCY and check again. |
| `too_large` | A limit in {doc} is too large to evaluate within this tool's limits. | Check this limit of {doc} by hand. |
| `unsigned_receipt` | {doc} is a plain unsigned record, not a signed token, so it proves nothing about who issued it. | Ask {party} for {doc} as a signed receipt. |
| `aud_missing` | {doc} does not name the recipient it was presented to. | Ask the agent provider why the mandate names no recipient (aud). |
| `nonce_missing` | {doc} carries no session value (nonce), so a replay cannot be ruled out. | Ask the agent provider why the mandate carries no nonce. |
| `declined` | {doc} says the transaction was declined. | Ask {party} what happened to the transaction. |
| `empty_checkout` | The merchant's checkout contains no items, so it cannot match the items the user allowed. | Ask the merchant for its signed checkout with the items that were bought. |
| `history_needed` | The user's mandate sets a cumulative limit (budget or number of uses), and the verifier was not told what had been spent or used before this payment. | Get what was already spent and how many payments were already made under this mandate from the mandate issuer's or payment processor's records, and check again with --prior-total MINOR_UNITS CURRENCY and --prior-uses N. |
| `occurrences_exceeded` | Together with the earlier payments you said were made under this mandate, this payment is more than the number of payments the user allowed. | Confirm the number of earlier payments with the mandate issuer's or payment processor's records; if it is right, ask the agent provider why its agent made one payment too many. |
| `not_expected` | No expected value was given, so this was not compared. | - |
| `agent_key_mismatch` | The agent key in the mandates is not the agent key you expected. | Ask the agent provider which agent key it uses and why the mandates name another one. |
| `checkout_id_mismatch` | The checkout in the bundle is not the checkout you expected. | Check that you have the bundle for the right order; ask the merchant which checkout this payment belongs to. |
| `merchant_id_mismatch` | The merchant in the bundle is not the merchant you expected. | Check that you have the bundle for the right merchant; ask the agent provider why the agent dealt with another merchant. |
| `total_mismatch` | The checkout total is not the total you expected. | Compare the expected total with the merchant's records and ask the merchant which total it charged. |
| `constraint_missing` | The user's mandate lacks a limit you required it to contain. | Ask the agent provider why the open mandate was issued without this limit. |

Overrides for specific checks:

| Check | Reason | Plain wording | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR05 | `declined` | The Payment Receipt says the payment was declined; on its own it shows that no money moved. | Treat the payment as not made unless the payment processor confirms a later successful attempt. |
| CR05 | `declined` | The Checkout Receipt says the merchant declined or failed the order. | Ask the merchant whether the order was declined and whether any payment for it was refunded. |
| PM39 | `budget_exceeded` | Together with the amount you said was already spent under this mandate, this payment exceeds the user's budget. | Confirm the earlier spend with the mandate issuer's or payment processor's records; if it is right, ask the agent provider why its agent approved a payment that takes the total over the user's budget. |
| CM04 | `unreferenced_disclosure` | Part of the user's shopping instructions was changed after they were signed. | Ask the agent provider for the user's original shopping instructions, exactly as they were issued. |
| CM04 | `duplicate_disclosure` | Part of the user's shopping instructions was changed after they were signed. | Ask the agent provider for the user's original shopping instructions, exactly as they were issued. |
